Nature, environment & conservation 2

Talk about nature under pressure in Thai. This second part starts with the joys — โลมา (dolphins), ผีเสื้อ (butterflies), a healthy ระบบนิเวศ (ecosystem) and อากาศบริสุทธิ์ (clean air) — then faces the problems: ฝุ่น (dust), หมอกควัน (haze), มลพิษ (pollution), ขยะพลาสติก (plastic waste), น้ำเสีย (wastewater), ไฟป่า (forest fires), deforestation and drought. All 18 sentences come with native-speed audio, English translations and word-by-word notes, so the environmental vocabulary sticks by ear.

The natural world

6 ฝุ่น…
ช่วงนี้ฝุ่น PM 2.5 หนักมาก ออกไปข้างนอกต้องใส่หน้ากาก
PM2.5 dust is really bad lately — you have to wear a mask going outside.

PM2.5 (fine-dust) pollution is a serious seasonal problem, worst from roughly December to April. The north — especially Chiang Mai — regularly tops global pollution rankings during burning season, and masks, air purifiers and the occasional school closure become routine.

Burning crop stubble and forest to clear land each dry season blankets the north in smog, the main driver of the region's PM2.5 spikes from February to April.

A rai (ไร่) is the Thai unit of land area, equal to 1,600 m² (0.16 ha). Dry-season wildfires routinely burn many thousands of rai across the northern forests.
